formation.title: The Franconian Circle
formation.text:
The disparate territories of Franconia (prince-bishoprics, margraviates, free cities, and knightly domains) have at last been drawn together under a single banner. But which tradition shall define this union?

The prince-bishops of Wurzburg and Bamberg offer the model of ecclesiastical authority, where spiritual conviction provides the foundation for temporal governance. Their cathedrals and residences anchor the region in faith and learning.

Alternatively, Nuremberg's master craftsmen represent a different path. Unburdened by guild restrictions, the city's workshops produce metalwork, clocks, and printed works that are the finest in the Empire. Their inventive spirit could transform Franconia into a center of innovation.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The bishops shall lead our people in faith and governance

modifiers.name: The Princes' Faith
modifiers.text: The prince-bishops of Franconia wield both crosier and sword, governing their domains as temporal lords no less than spiritual shepherds. Under their guidance, the faith binds the scattered territories into a single purpose.

options.text: Let Nuremberg's workshops light the way forward

modifiers.name: The Craftsmen's Spirit
modifiers.text: Nuremberg's master craftsmen answer not to guild halls but to the city council itself. This system of regulated innovation, where skill is rewarded and competition is fierce, has made the city's workshops the envy of Europe.

advances.name: Stem Duchy Heritage
advances.text: Franconia was the homeland of the Salian dynasty, whose kings and emperors ruled the Empire from this heartland of East Francia.

advances.name: The Ritterschaft
advances.text: The Imperial Knights of Franconia form a distinct martial class, owing allegiance directly to the Emperor rather than to any territorial prince.

advances.name: Main River Viticulture
advances.text: The slopes along the Main River support Europe's largest medieval wine region, with over 40,000 hectares under cultivation by the 14th century.

advances.name: Cathedral Foundations
advances.text: The cathedrals of Bamberg and Wurzburg anchor Franconia's spiritual identity, serving as centers of learning, art, and ecclesiastical authority.

event.title: The Cathedrals of Franconia
event.text:
The great cathedrals of Bamberg and Wurzburg stand as monuments to centuries of Franconian devotion. The Bamberg Cathedral, founded by the sainted Emperor Henry II in 1007, houses the enigmatic Bamberger Reiter: the first monumental equestrian sculpture since antiquity, a crowned horseman whose true identity remains a mystery.

In Wurzburg, the Romanesque cathedral dedicated to St. Kilian anchors the spiritual life of Lower Franconia. Together, these houses of God are not merely places of worship but seats of learning, repositories of art, and symbols of the intertwined spiritual and temporal authority that defines Franconian governance.

options.text: Their spires shall endure as long as Franconia itself

advances.name: Nuremberg Metalcraft
advances.text: Nuremberg's master craftsmen produce metalwork of unrivaled precision, from church bells and armor to scissors, jewelry, and nails, all under the city council's watchful eye.

advances.name: Episcopal Governance
advances.text: The prince-bishops of Franconia wield both spiritual and temporal authority, governing their territories as ecclesiastical princes of the Empire.

advances.name: Bamberg Cultural Flowering
advances.text: Bamberg's cultural renaissance, from the enigmatic Horseman sculpture to the patronage of arts and learning, elevates Franconia's reputation across Christendom.

advances.name: Imperial City Charters
advances.text: Nuremberg, Rothenburg, and Schweinfurt hold charters as free imperial cities, answering only to the Emperor and governing their own trade and justice.

advances.name: Nuremberg Printing
advances.text: The Koberger workshop in Nuremberg produces the Nuremberg Chronicle and other masterworks, making the city a center of the European printing revolution.

advances.name: Circle Administration
advances.text: The Franconian Kreistag coordinates defense, coinage, and peacekeeping across the Circle's diverse territories of bishops, margraves, and free cities.

event.title: The Founding of the Franconian Circle
event.text:
On 2 July 1500, the Imperial Diet at Augsburg established the Franconian Circle as one of the six original administrative districts of the Empire. This institution gives the patchwork of Franconian territories a collective voice: a Kreistag where prince-bishops, margraves, free cities, and imperial knights may coordinate defense, regulate coinage, and preserve the Landfrieden.

The Circle's strength lies in cooperation among its diverse members. But some see an opportunity to assert Franconian independence within the Empire's framework, building military capacity that serves our interests first.

modifiers.name: Circle Cooperation
modifiers.text: The Franconian Circle functions as a model of imperial cooperation, its Kreistag bringing together diverse estates to maintain peace and coordinate defense.

options.text: We must look to our own strength

modifiers.name: Circle Self-Reliance
modifiers.text: Rather than depend on imperial structures, Franconia builds its own military capacity, ensuring that the Circle can defend itself on its own terms.

advances.name: Peasant War Legacy
advances.text: The devastating Peasants' War of 1525 and Florian Geyer's Black Troop left lasting lessons about the strength and fury of Franconia's common people.

event.title: The Peasants' War in Franconia
event.text:
The spring of 1525 has brought revolution to Franconia. Peasant bands under leaders like Florian Geyer and his fearsome Black Troop have swept through the Tauber valley, storming castles and demanding rights long denied. The greatest peasant army in all Germany has assembled before Wurzburg, threatening the very seat of episcopal power.

The rebellion will be crushed; of that there is little doubt. But the memory of Geyer's Black Troop and the Twelve Articles will linger. We must decide how to rebuild: with concessions that address legitimate grievances, or with the iron hand of noble authority reasserted.

options.text: Address the root causes of discontent

modifiers.name: Peasant Concessions
modifiers.text: In the aftermath of the Peasants' War, measured reforms address some of the grievances that drove men like Florian Geyer to rebellion.

options.text: Restore order with an iron hand

modifiers.name: Restored Authority
modifiers.text: The nobility reasserts its prerogatives with force, ensuring that the disorder of 1525 shall never be repeated.

advances.name: Cannon Foundries
advances.text:
Nuremberg's metalworking expertise extends naturally to arms production, with foundries casting cannons and forging weaponry for the Empire's armies.

Available in: Meisterhaus

advances.name: Confessional Frontier
advances.text: Franconia sits on the fault line between Catholic and Protestant territories, forcing its rulers to navigate confessional tensions with pragmatism.

advances.name: Kreisarmee Reforms
advances.text: The Circle's military forces are professionalized into a proper Kreisarmee, drawing disciplined soldiers from the cities and trained levies from the countryside.

advances.name: Nuremberg Clockworks
advances.text:
Peter Henlein's portable spring-driven clocks, the 'Nuremberg Eggs,' represent the pinnacle of precision engineering and make the city famous across Europe.

Available in: Meisterhaus

advances.name: Landfrieden Enforcement
advances.text: The Circle takes responsibility for maintaining the Imperial Peace within its borders, suppressing feuds and highway robbery to secure trade routes. Mounted men on the cities' pay ride the roads and escort the merchants.

advances.name: Franconian Baroque
advances.text: Balthasar Neumann's masterful Wurzburg Residenz and the region's baroque churches represent a flowering of Franconian artistic achievement. Their windows and mirrors come from the court's own glassworks in the Steigerwald.

advances.name: Standing Kreiskompanie
advances.text: Permanent garrison forces maintain order and defend the Circle's borders, equipped with artillery from Franconia's renowned foundries.

advances.name: Commercial Code
advances.text: A unified code of commercial law regulates trade across Franconia's fragmented patchwork of territories, reducing friction and encouraging mercantile activity.

advances.name: Episcopal Scholarship
advances.text: The University of Wurzburg and Bamberg's learned traditions produce scholars and administrators who serve both church and state.

advances.name: Civic Enlightenment
advances.text: Franconia's urban tradition of civic self-governance provides fertile ground for Enlightenment ideals of reason, education, and constitutional reform.

advances.name: Industrial Modernization
advances.text:
The centuries-old crafts tradition transforms into modern manufacturing as Franconian workshops adopt industrial methods and new materials.

Available in: Meisterhaus

advances.name: National Integration
advances.text: The bewildering patchwork of Franconian territories (bishoprics, margraviates, free cities, and knightly domains) begins to coalesce into a unified whole.

advances.name: Constitutional Reforms
advances.text: Liberal governance replaces the old regime of princely absolutism and clerical authority, bringing representative institutions to Franconia.

destiny.name: Franconia's Destiny
destiny.text: The Franconian Circle has been forged. Now its destiny must be fulfilled: whether through the authority of the crosier or the ingenuity of the workshop.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: Franconia's Destiny
event.text: The Franconian Circle stands united at last, its disparate territories joined under a single vision. Whether guided by the crosier or the craftsman's hammer, the choices we make now will shape our path through the ages to come.

destiny.name: Archiepiscopal Authority
destiny.text: Secure the great archbishopric of Mainz and the monastery of Fulda, placing Franconia at the spiritual heart of the Empire.

conditions.text: The Princes' Faith path has been chosen
Own Mainz, or a subject owns it
Own Fulda, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: Archiepiscopal Authority
event.text: Mainz has fallen under our control: the seat of the Primate of Germany, the premier archbishopric of the Holy Roman Empire. Together with the ancient monastery of Fulda, these ecclesiastical foundations place Franconia at the spiritual heart of Christendom north of the Alps. The prince-bishops now speak with a voice that commands respect across the Empire.

destiny.name: See of the Primate
destiny.text: Bring the three Rhenish archbishoprics (Mainz, Cologne, and Trier) under Franconian authority, commanding the prince-electors who crown emperors, and build Würzburg into a residence fit for a primate.

conditions.text: Own Cologne, or a subject owns it
Own Trier, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 50
We own Würzburg and its development is at least 40

event.title: See of the Primate
event.text:
The three Rhenish archbishoprics (Mainz, Cologne, and Trier), the prince-electors who crown emperors and shape the fate of the Empire, all now acknowledge Franconian authority. This concentration of ecclesiastical power is unprecedented since the days of Charlemagne himself.

We may use this authority to bind the Rhineland's diverse peoples into a centralized whole, or we may invest in the episcopal courts themselves, making them centers of learning and conversion that transform culture from within.

options.text: Unite the Rhineland under one authority

modifiers.name: Rhenish Unity
modifiers.text: The lands along the Rhine are drawn together under Franconian episcopal authority, creating a centralized power bloc at the heart of the Empire.

options.text: Invest in our episcopal courts and schools

modifiers.name: Episcopal Courts
modifiers.text: The prince-bishops' courts become centers of learning and ecclesiastical administration, shaping the culture and faith of their subjects.

destiny.name: Defender of the Faith
destiny.text: Control the four great German archbishoprics from Aachen to Salzburg and take up the cause of the confession, establishing Franconia as the paramount spiritual authority in Christendom. This stage cannot be completed before the Age of Reformation.

conditions.text: Own Salzburg, or a subject owns it
Own Aachen, or a subject owns it
Reformation or later
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: Defender of the Faith
event.text:
From Aachen, where Charlemagne was crowned, to Salzburg, where Boniface planted the cross among the pagans, the great archbishoprics of the German lands all stand under Franconian stewardship. No realm in Christendom commands such a concentration of spiritual authority.

This power invites a choice: shall Franconia serve as the sword of the faith, a Catholic champion ready to defend the Church against all threats? Or shall we follow the path of the Landfrieden: using our authority to impose peace and stability across the fractured landscape of the Empire?

options.text: We shall be the sword of the faith

modifiers.name: Catholic Champion
modifiers.text: Franconia stands as the sword of the Catholic faith, its armies ready to defend the Church and impose its will on heretics and unbelievers.

options.text: We shall be the guarantors of peace

modifiers.name: Prince of Peace
modifiers.text: Following the tradition of the Landfrieden, Franconia uses its spiritual authority to mediate disputes and maintain stability across the fractured Empire.

destiny.name: Imperial Free Commerce
destiny.text: Secure Frankfurt's great trade fairs and let the fair town grow into a city of money changers and merchants, transforming Franconia into the commercial heart of the Empire. Requires 1,000 gold in the treasury.

conditions.text: The Craftsmen's Spirit path has been chosen
Frankfurt is ours and has grown into a city
Gold at least 1000
Stability at least 25

event.title: Imperial Free Commerce
event.text: Frankfurt's great trade fairs now operate under the Franconian banner. The city where emperors are crowned and merchants from across Europe gather to exchange goods stands as proof that Franconian craftsmanship and commercial acumen can match any rival. With Frankfurt grown into a city of money changers, the future belongs to those who master the flow of capital.

options.text: Let commerce flourish under our watch

destiny.name: Workshop of the Empire
destiny.text: Build Nuremberg into the Empire's foremost manufacturing city, with tools flowing from our workshops to markets across Central Europe.

conditions.text: Gold at least 2000
We own Nuremberg and its development is at least 36
A market the country is in

children.text: Tools is produced in the market
Tools is traded in the market

event.title: Workshop of the Empire
event.text:
Franconia's workshops have become the engine of the Empire's economy. From Nuremberg's precision instruments to the trade goods flowing through our markets, our craftsmen set the standard that others strive to match. The tools made in our cities build the buildings, forge the weapons, and drive the machinery of progress across Central Europe.

We may deepen our mastery of craftsmanship itself, investing in the Meister tradition that ensures quality above all else, or we may leverage our position to secure trade fair privileges that draw commerce from across the continent.

options.text: Invest in our masters and their craft

modifiers.name: Meister Tradition
modifiers.text: The Franconian master craftsman system produces goods of such quality that armies and workshops across the Empire rely on them, though the finest work demands its price in materials.

options.text: Secure trade fair privileges for our cities

modifiers.name: Trade Fair Privilege
modifiers.text: Imperial privileges grant Franconian cities the right to hold great trade fairs, drawing merchants and capital from across Europe.

destiny.name: The Industrious Revolution
destiny.text: Dominate the great commercial hubs of Augsburg and Leipzig, raise court glassworks in two of our forests, and lead the transformation from craft workshop to manufacture.

conditions.text: Own Augsburg, or a subject owns it
Own Leipzig, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000
A Hofglashütte stands in at least 2 of our locations

event.title: The Industrious Revolution
event.text:
The transformation is complete. From medieval workshop to modern manufactory, Franconia has led the way in the industrious revolution that remakes the old order. Augsburg's banking houses and Leipzig's trade fairs now orbit around Franconian enterprise, and the hum of machinery has replaced the ring of the blacksmith's hammer.

This new power demands a new order. Shall we embrace the factory and the furnace, driving forward with industrial ambition regardless of the old ways it displaces? Or shall we channel our commercial strength into building a new kind of civic society, where merchants and craftsmen govern themselves in the spirit of the free imperial cities?

modifiers.name: Manufactory Revolution
modifiers.text: The transformation from workshop to factory proceeds at pace, though the disruption of old economic patterns makes the realm less eager for costly wars.

options.text: Let the merchant spirit govern our republic

modifiers.name: Merchant Republic Spirit
modifiers.text: The civic traditions of the free imperial cities inspire a new model of governance where commercial interests and liberal ideals shape the state.

units.name: Franconian Ritter
units.text: Heavy cavalry of the Imperial Knights, drawn from the Franconian Ritterschaft and owing allegiance directly to the Emperor.

units.name: Nuremberg Stadtsoldat
units.text: Disciplined city soldiers raised from the burghers and garrison of Nuremberg, trained under the city council's military system.

units.name: Einspännige
units.text: Mounted men on the permanent pay of the Franconian cities, each serving with a single horse. They ride escort for the merchants on the road to the Frankfurt fair and run down those who break the peace.

units.name: Franconian Feldbatterie
units.text: Field artillery batteries cast in Nuremberg's renowned foundries, combining superior Franconian metalwork with the latest gunnery techniques.

buildings.name: Meisterhaus
buildings.text: A Nuremberg master craftsman's workshop where skilled artisans produce metalwork, tools, and precision instruments under the city council's regulated system.

buildings.name: Prince-Bishop's Residenz
buildings.text: The seat of episcopal governance, where the prince-bishop exercises both spiritual authority and temporal lordship over his territories.

buildings.name: Weinberghaus
buildings.text: A Franconian wine estate on the sun-facing slopes of the Main valley, producing the distinctive wines that once made this Europe's largest viticultural region.

buildings.name: Druckerei
buildings.text: A Nuremberg printing house where master printers produce books, pamphlets, and broadsheets that spread knowledge and reform across the Empire.

buildings.name: Hofglashütte
buildings.text: A court glassworks in the forest, of the kind Balthasar Neumann ran at Schleichach to glaze and mirror the Residenz. What the court does not need is sold abroad.

where.text: Sand is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Hochstift
buildings.text: An episcopal cathedral-palace complex where the prince-bishop exercises both spiritual and temporal authority, combining a great church with a school of theology and a seat of governance.

buildings.name: Handelshaus
buildings.text: A Franconian merchant trading house that coordinates commerce, warehousing, and manufacturing under one roof, embodying the industrious spirit of the free imperial cities.

list.name: Fränkischer Kreistag
list.text: The assembly of the Franconian Imperial Circle, instituted under the 1500 reform of Maximilian I and convening at Nuremberg under a duumviral directorate of the Bishop of Bamberg and the Margrave of Brandenburg-Ansbach. The Kreistag matriculated each estate's contribution to the imperial register, elected judges to the Reichskammergericht, supervised the Franconian coinage, and executed the Landfrieden. Of the ten Imperial Circles it was the most cohesive and the only one to maintain a standing Kreistroops levy until 1806.

list.name: Domkapitel
list.text: The cathedral chapters of Bamberg and Würzburg, which elected the prince-bishops via Wahlkapitulationen, binding electoral capitulations, that constrained episcopal taxation, legislation, and appointments. From the 15th century the Domkapitel of Würzburg routinely co-governed the Hochstift; the Bamberg chapter ran episcopal justice through its Hofgericht and licensed the diocesan press. No prince-bishop could circumvent his canons, and the chapter's seat outlasted every individual bishop.

conditions.text: Catholicism religion
Any of

list.name: Innerer Rat
list.text: The Lesser Council of Nuremberg, formalised around 1320 and closed to a roster of forty-two patrician families by the dance statute of 1521. Its septemvirate of Ältere Herren and triumvirate of Oberste Hauptleute supervised every city office; from Sigismund's charter of 1424 the council held the Imperial Regalia at the Heilig-Geist-Spital and staged the annual Heiltumsweisung that anchored Nuremberg's trade fair. A small oligarchy ran the Empire's wealthiest free city for almost five centuries.

conditions.text: Owns Nuremberg

list.name: Ritterkanton
list.text: The Franconian canton of the Imperial Knights, organised under Maximilian I around 1500 and formalised in 1577 as one of three Ritterkreise. The six cantons of Franconia (Odenwald, Gebürg, Steigerwald, Altmühl, Baunach, and Rhön-Werra) maintained their own captains, archives, and matriculation lists. They paid voluntary Charitativsubsidien to the emperor in lieu of taxes, and their lands stood exempt from any territorial sovereign. The Reichsritter formed a nobility-within-a-nobility, structurally hostile to centralisation.

list.name: Landfriede
list.text: The regional public-peace ordinance, running in Franconia from the Würzburg Landfriede of 1287 through Maximilian's Ewiger Landfriede of 1495 and administered after 1500 by the Kreistag's Landfriedenswahrung commissioners. It outlawed feuds between estates, proclaimed peace on the great trade roads from Nuremberg to Frankfurt and from Würzburg to Erfurt, and pursued Friedensbrecher through the Reichskammergericht. Where it held, the Franconian markets thrived; where it failed, the Reichsritter resumed their raiding.
